answer: An agent economy can make identity valuable only after it earns a kernel of trust: each agent posts a bond and receives a limited orchard of work credits, replenished when independent counterparties confirm completed tasks. Repeated failures slash the bond and reduce future credit. Creating many identities does not multiply useful capacity, because each needs its own capital and must attract costly, independent endorsements; splitting a fixed stake across fake agents leaves each too weak to trade. A durable anchor is the stake at risk, not the claimed identity.
